mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national registrar or authorized notary in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country trade registry or corporate registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record extract (extrait de casier judiciaire) for each proposed manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of justice or competent criminal record authority in country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified bank reference and source-of-funds confirmation for subscription of share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution holding the shareholder deposit account

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney or written instruction to the Luxembourg notary, if any
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PoA grantor before a notary public in country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the UN Security Council sanctions list, the OFAC SDN list, the Luxembourg CSSF/FIU recommendations, and a reputable commercial PEP database. Enhanced due diligence applies for any PEP, adverse media hit, inconsistent source-of-funds, or residence in high-risk third countries. Results must be documented and made available to the Luxembourg notary and any AML/CFT obliged entity acting as the onboarding intermediary.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accessible via the official online portal lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name may be composed in one of Luxembourg's official administrative languages (French, German, or Luxembourgish) and must be written in the Latin alphabet. Any non-Latin script must be transliterated. The legal form designation 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'S.à r.l.' must be included as part of the corporate name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg when used to imply official government sponsorship
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation may be extended by a written application to the RCS before expiration. If the RCS rejects the proposed name, the applicant receives a reasoned negative decision. The applicant may file an administrative appeal with the commercial chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within 40 days of notification, pursuant to Article 8 of the RCS Law of 19 December 2002, and/or may submit a revised name to the RCS for a fresh reservation cycle.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Strictly limited. Luxembourg law requires a registered office and an actual establishment on Luxembourg soil. A professional domiciliation arrangement with a supervised domiciliation agent is accepted, but a virtual or post-office-only address is not permissible. For an outsourced virtual CFO practice, the tax authority will expect sufficient substance, including local management ability, administration presence, and business records held within Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate — approximately 25% likelihood within the first 36 months of operation. The likelihood increases to 35% if a domiciliation agent is used and no lease exists, or if intra-group invoicing and cross-border services exceed €500,000 in the first fiscal year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Articles 710-1 to 710-26 for SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS); Law of 2 September 2011 on Business Establishment Permits
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (Acte constitutif) containing the Articles of Incorporation (Statuts), filed with the RCS and published in the official electronic gazette (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is EUR 12,000 for a SARL, fully subscribed and paid-up. The cash contribution must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (attestation de blocage) with a Luxembourg credit institution; the bank certificate is delivered to the notary prior to execution of the incorporation deed
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the incorporator's subscription to the issued share capital of the company, in the amount and form set forth in the draft articles and share subscription schedule, is hereby approved and ratified. RESOLVED: That the registered office of the company be established at [Address] in the City of Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, effective immediately. RESOLVED: That [Name] be and is hereby appointed as Manager (Gérant) of the company, with full powers to manage, represent and bind the company in accordance with the laws of Luxembourg and the Articles of Incorporation. RESOLVED: That the Manager is authorized to make all statutory filings, open bank accounts, and complete the company's formation, licensing and ongoing administrative obligations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name verification and drafting of articles of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS e-Services and Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the availability and legal compliance of the intended corporate name through the RCS online business directory. Instruct a Luxembourg notary to prepare the draft Articles of Incorporation (Statuts) containing the SARL name, registered office address, share capital breakdown, object clause limited to ISIC 6920 services, management provisions, and transfer of quota restrictions.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of incorporators and managers
Planned paid-up capital proof (bank account statement or letter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, promptly select a second available name and file a revised draft; if the notary identifies omissions under the 1915 Law, amend the articles accordingly and obtain incorporator approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the escrowed share capital account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account (compte bloqué) in the name of the SARL en constitution at a Luxembourg bank. Deposit the full minimum capital of EUR 12,000 or more and request the bank's attestation de blocage confirming the deposit and the blocking of funds until formal incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional AML/CTF due diligence, supply the requested corporate and beneficial ownership evidence; if the bank refuses the account, engage an alternative Luxembourg bank and repeat the escrow deposit before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial execution of the incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Schedule the execution meeting before the notary. The incorporators (or their lawyer-in-fact under a notarized power of attorney) sign the notarial deed; the notary verifies legal capacity, capital deposit certificate, and gift/tax compliance, then authenticates the Articles of Incorporation. The deed includes the appointment of the first Manager and the registered office.
required_dossiers: Proof of residential address of managers
Certificate of legal form if a corporate shareholder is involved
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses execution for statutory deficiencies, file a corrected deed or supplementary instrument; resolve any issue in the capital deposit certificate before final execution; reschedule execution once cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified notarial deed and the required statutory filings with the RCS through the LBR online filing system. Pay the registration fee and obtain the RCS registration number and legal entity business identification number. The RCS will verify the compliance of the deed and issue the certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial incorporation deed
Registered office address agreement (domiciliation contract or lease)
Proof of payment of filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or refusal, respond within 15 calendar days with the required clarifications; if the defect affects the deed itself, obtain a notarial rectification act from the original notary and resubmit to the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of incorporation notice in the official electronic gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically transmits the registration data and deed extracts to the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations) for publication. Monitor the gazette entry to confirm third-party legal effectiveness of the incorporation and the manager's powers.
required_dossiers: Extract of the notarial deed with publication text
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, contact the LBR operational support; if the published notice contains errors, file an application for rectification with the RCS within one month of the first publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Business Establishment Department (Ministère de l'Économie, Service des autorisations d'établissement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a complete application for the establishment permit required for commercial service activities, including outsourced CFO and accounting services. Provide proof of the manager's good character (criminal record extract) and relevant professional experience. The permit authorizes the continued exercise of the business activity within the Grand Duchy.
required_dossiers: Criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) of each managing officer
Evidence of professional qualifications or exemption
Commercial lease agreement for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit is refused, appeal administratively to the Minister of the Economy within 40 days, or submit for reconsideration with additional evidence of qualifications; in the alternative, resort to the administrative court within three months of the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enrollment with social security and VAT registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the CCSS to obtain social security numbers for the employees and the company. Submit the corresponding registrations to the AED for Luxembourg VAT purposes, declaring the object of ISIC 6920 and expected turnover.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number and incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed or documents are rejected, contact the competent CCSS or AED desk to correct the file; if late-filing penalties are threatened, present evidence of submission within statutory window and request penalty remission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal and occupational safety clearance for the physical premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commune (municipality) and Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the municipal location authorization and coordinate with the commune and ITM for any necessary workplace inspections. For an office-based virtual CFO activity, ensure occupational safety, electrical safety, and emergency exit compliance; if the building lease requires, obtain the fire safety certificate from the local fire authority.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement for the registered office
Floor plan and structural load certification if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality or ITM identifies non-compliance, execute the corrective measures within the stated time limit; if clearance is denied, appeal to the local administrative commission or the Ministry of Labour within 15 days of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Business Establishment Department (Service des autorisations d'établissement)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Establishment Permit (Autorisation d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 4 – Exempt (office-based accounting/consulting activity; no EIA or environmental registration required)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions for virtual CFO services; compliance with municipal wastewater discharge limits, segregated waste collection via approved waste contractors, and administrative thresholds under the Luxembourg environmental classification law of 19 July 2013

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) or the competent commune; structural load inspection for office premises; occupational safety clearance from the Labour Inspection (Inspection du Travail et des Mines, ITM) including electrical conformity and emergency exit certification

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of Finance — Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de la TVA (Luxembourg VAT Authority) for indirect taxes; official filing and registration portals are myGuichet.lu, impotsdirects.public.lu, vat.public.lu, and the eCDF electronic VAT filing interface.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident establishing or registering a Luxembourg SARL obtains its statutory identifiers in a five-step sequence: (1) notarized incorporation and approval of the articles of association, followed by registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés — RCS), which allocates the RCS registration number; (2) filing of the legal publication formalities and deposit of the annual accounts; (3) registration with the social security authorities (Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale — CCSS), producing the employer identification number; (4) application to the ACD for the Luxembourg national tax number (numéro d'identification national / matricule) used for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; and (5) application to the Administration de la TVA for the Luxembourg VAT identification number (prefix LU + 8 digits), which is mandatory whenever taxable turnover exceeds EUR 35,000 or, irrespective of threshold, when taxable supplies are made in Luxembourg. Non-established foreign operators supplying services exclusively to Luxembourg taxable persons remain outside the Luxembourg VAT net under the reverse-charge mechanism; a foreign entity making domestic taxable supplies in Luxembourg must appoint a fiscal representative if it is established in a third country that has no mutual-assistance agreement with Luxembourg. All registrations and filings are executed electronically through myGuichet.lu and eCDF using authenticated e-Citizen or professional e-identity credentials.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg is a codified civil-law jurisdiction and does not offer any 'check-the-box' pass-through election. The SARL is mandatorily a resident corporate taxpayer subject to entity-level taxation on worldwide income, with territorial relief available for certain foreign branch income and gains. Available opt-in regimes include: (i) the participation exemption for qualifying dividend income and capital gains under Article 166 LIR, subject to an advance ruling application; (ii) the tax consolidation election (intégration fiscale) for corporate income tax and municipal business tax purposes between a Luxembourg parent and its directly or indirectly 95%-owned resident subsidiaries; (iii) the VAT grouping election ('assujetti unique') allowing financially and legally connected Luxembourg taxable persons to be treated as a single taxable person; (iv) advance pricing agreements and unilateral tax rulings on transfer pricing, substance, and hybrid-mismatch neutrality; and (v) anti-hybrid and ATAD-driven classification results, which are mandatory and not elective. Pass-through classification of a SARL is legally unavailable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), implemented pursuant to the Luxembourg VAT law (Loi du 12 février 1979 sur la TVA) and the EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 (annual taxable turnover exclusive of VAT; below this threshold the small-business franchise exemption may apply, while mandatory VAT registration is triggered once the threshold is exceeded; non-established suppliers remain registerable irrespective of turnover when making a taxable supply in Luxembourg, subject to reverse-charge relief for B2B supplies).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: There is no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based pre-clearance regime in force for B2B invoices in Luxembourg. Electronic invoicing between private businesses remains optional; where used, e-invoices must comply with the European standard EN 16931 and applicable EU e-invoicing rules. B2G e-invoicing to Luxembourg public authorities is mandatory via the Peppol network. All taxable persons must issue VAT-compliant invoices, retain them in their original format for at least ten years, and transmit the underlying turnover data through the periodic VAT return, the recapitulative statement, and Intrastat/introduction declarations, all filed electronically via the eCDF interface and myGuichet.lu.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: the export exemption (0% VAT) under the Luxembourg VAT law applies only where (a) goods are dispatched or transported out of the EU by the supplier, the customer, or a third party acting in their name; (b) the goods physically leave the EU, generally within 90 days of dispatch (extendable to 12 months for approved movements); and (c) the exporter holds the customs export declaration validated by Luxembourg customs together with transport documents proving EU exit. For services: zero-rating is achieved through the place-of-supply rule — B2B services supplied to a taxable customer established outside the EU are deemed supplied outside Luxembourg and therefore remain outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT; the supplier must evidence the customer's non-EU business establishment through a valid foreign VAT identification number or equivalent business-register proof, the service contract, itemized professional invoices, and the bank settlement trail. Where the customer is a non-taxable person outside the EU, professional consulting and accounting services are generally taxed in Luxembourg unless a specific derogation or use-and-enjoyment rule applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — fully validated electronic Single Administrative Document (SAD/EAD) accepted by the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration
Transport evidence — original Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note showing dispatch from Luxembourg and physical exit of the goods from the EU within the statutory period
Commercial documentation — signed sales contract, pro forma or commercial invoice, packing list, and stated Incoterms
Non-EU customer status evidence — foreign VAT registration number or official extract from the customer's business register, required for zero-rating of services
Inward remittance certificate and corresponding bank statements evidencing receipt of the export consideration from the foreign buyer within the repatriation deadline
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg's VAT and direct tax authorities audit zero-rated export claims under a general five-year assessment limitation period, extended to ten years where fraud or willful omission is established. If the 0% rate is applied without complete documentary substantiation, the supply is recharacterized as taxable in Luxembourg, VAT is reassessed at the standard rate, default interest accrues from the due date, and administrative fines are imposed for each infringement. Deliberate fraudulent zero-rating — including fictitious exports, falsified transport documents, or sham non-EU customer structures — constitutes criminal tax fraud, exposing the legal representatives and any appointed jointly and severally liable fiscal representative to criminal fines and imprisonment, retrospective clawback of VAT credits, and professional disqualification, in addition to the reassessed VAT and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) (Central Bank of Luxembourg)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a Eurozone member in which both current and capital account transactions are fully convertible by virtue of EU free movement of capital (art. 63 TFEU). The Euro has no purchase or sale restrictions; profit remittances from a SARL are subject only to the 15% statutory dividend withholding tax (reduced by tax treaty or parent-subsidiary exemption) and to underlying substance requirements. Neither central bank notification nor exchange control approval is required for bona fide remittances. Non-resident shareholders and lenders may convert and repatriate funds freely, but the BCL collects balance-of-payments statistical data on cross-border flows exceeding EUR 100,000.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no export proceeds surrender or conversion duty; the mandatory conversion ratio is 0% and there is no statutory deadline for repatriation or conversion of export receipts. Exporters must, however, support BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting for flows above EUR 100,000 and retain export invoices, bank statements and SWIFT confirmations for the general 5-year documentation period under the Luxembourg AML/CFT law of 12 November 2004.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Medium for operational treasury flows, Low for statutory capital receipt. A non-Luxembourg EMI such as Wise may passport into Luxembourg under PSD2 to provide transaction accounts, but it cannot deliver the credit-institution block-attestation required by Luxembourg notaries to verify full payment of the SARL's minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 into an account opened in the company's name. An EMI may be used for ancillary collection and disbursement purposes provided its safeguarding account is held with an EU credit institution, but it must not be the sole treasury rail for the regulated accounting and tax service activities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Generally mandatory for the first account opening where a non-resident gérant or UBO is a signatory; remote opening is possible only under CSSF-compliant videoconference KYC, using an EIDAS-qualified certificate or a comparable eID, and subject to the bank's internal higher-risk rules. The gérant must physically appear before the Luxembourg notary for the incorporation deed; after registration, the blocked capital account may be released upon a bank instruction supported by the notarially authenticated deed and RCS certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident gérant/UBO domiciled in a high-risk third country with no prior Luxembourg banking relationship.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised passport copy, RCS company certificate, UBO register declaration, proof of tax residence, reference letters from existing banks, source-of-wealth statement, and evidence of physical business substance in the home jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large recurring multi-currency receipts from Stripe/Wise aggregated to sub-merchants without clear service-level evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed engagement agreements with clients, merchant agreements with Stripe and Wise, platform settlement reconciliation reports, complete ledger bookkeeping, VAT registration certificate, and a written statement confirming that no client funds are held, safeguarded or routed on behalf of third parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office located only at a domiciliation or virtual-office provider for a virtual CFO activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Physical co-working or office lease in Luxembourg, payroll and social security registrations, outsourcing agreement with a regulated Luxembourg corporate service provider, board resolutions, business plan, client service schedule, and named staff with defined responsibilities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Share capital financed through a shareholder loan or cryptocurrency assets with ambiguous source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital blocked-account certificate, sworn declaration of lawful origin, shareholder bank statements showing accumulated savings or salary, loan agreement with amortisation schedule, and verification of the disposal chain of any crypto or other liquid assets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immediate outbound disbursement request to subcontractors and software vendors before the RCS commercial register entry is fully effective.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chronology of incorporation steps, notarised deed, RCS certificate, registered agent agreement, vendor contracts and quotes, invoice forecast, platform business reports, and written confirmation of each disbursement's commercial purpose.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder injections must be wired to the SARL's EUR blocked account (LU IBAN) opened at the incorporating Luxembourg bank before the notary executes the deed. For EEA investors, use TARGET2 or SEPA Credit Transfer with remittance 'LU-SARL-ISIC-6920 share capital contribution'; for non-EEA investors, use SWIFT MT103 to the Luxembourg bank BIC, with field 70 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / SUBSCRIPTION', the company's LEI if available, and the notary file reference. The account remains designated as blocked funds and is released only upon production of the registration certificate issued by the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For service-sector disbursements, the standard rail is SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR for counterparties within the EEA; for non-SEPA or non-EUR, use SWIFT MT103 or MT202 COV with the relevant invoice number and remittance purpose code 'Service Fees' or 'Business Travel' as applicable. Trade finance instruments such as a Commercial Letter of Credit are normally reserved for physical goods transactions; for matched procurement flows a Bank Payment Obligation may be used. All disbursements must be supported by vendor invoices and by the treasury mandate approved by the gérant or statutory board.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF transaction mismatches, generally with tenors up to 12 or 24 months
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid currencies, only where an underlying commercial exposure requiring settlement in an inconvertible currency is fully evidenced
Cross-currency swaps and FX swaps for long-term balance-sheet or net-investment hedging and asset-liability matching

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (financial statements) deposit with the Luxembourg commercial register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval and no later than seven months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the SARL to administrative fines and court-ordered daily penalty payments (astreinte); repeated non-filing can trigger judicial strike-off (radiation) from the RCS and personal liability of the manager.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SARL, the e-filed return must be submitted by 31 December of the year following the tax period; paper-filed returns must be lodged earlier unless a formal extension is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a penalty of up to 25% of the assessed tax plus monthly default interest; deliberate omission exposes responsible managers to criminal fiscal sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership information (annual RBE confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once each calendar year, calculated from the initial RBE registration date or the last confirmation date, and within one month after any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is punishable by criminal fines for legal persons up to EUR 250,000 and registration of non-compliance on the RBE; continued non-confirmation can ultimately expose the SARL to registry strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is compulsory if the SARL exceeds at least two of the three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total above approximately EUR 4,400,000, net turnover above approximately EUR 8,800,000, or 50 average employees; audit is also compulsory for public-interest undertakings, regulated financial-sector entities, and on resident shareholder request in accordance with the Luxembourg companies law
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts and consolidated accounts, as amended and transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; the SARL may elect to prepare statutory accounts under IFRS as endorsed by the EU

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must keep its beneficial ownership data in the RBE accurate at all times. At least once each calendar year, the responsible manager must confirm through the LBR online portal that the recorded beneficial-ownership information remains correct or has been updated. Any transfer of shares that changes beneficial ownership must additionally be declared within one month. The manager is personally liable for false incomplete or untimely confirmations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Managerial Resolutions
Minute Book (shareholders' resolutions and managerial decisions)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City combined effective rate, comprising 17% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge, and 6.75% municipal business tax; the aggregate may vary marginally across communes)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective rate on qualifying dividend and capital-gain income under the participation exemption; 80% exemption on eligible IP income under the Luxembourg IP box (effective rate approximately 5%); 20% investment tax credit for qualifying new tangible assets; additional R&D refundable credit of 25% to 50%
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory time limit; however, a change of shareholding exceeding 25% may trigger recapture if the loss carryforward is claimed for tax avoidance)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 740 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités et l'impôt commercial communal), filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu through the e-filing portal of the Administration des contributions directes; separate net-wealth tax return (Formulaire 840) may be required
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 March of the year following the fiscal year-end for paper returns; the tax administration usually grants an automatic extension for e-filed returns, commonly to 30 June, with further extensions available upon reasoned request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the SARL, registered seat, RCS number (Registre de commerce et des sociétés), Luxembourg TIN (matricule), and contact details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable for a resident SARL; if the entity is tax-resident in Luxembourg, this box is mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the fiscal year being reported
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the accounting period recognized by the Luxembourg tax authorities; a non-resident company filing for a Luxembourg permanent establishment must align the period with the Luxembourg PE accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Résultat commercial / Commercial accounting profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net book profit or loss before tax as shown in the annual statutory accounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident company, only the Luxembourg-source profit attributable to the local PE is entered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses (penalties, excessive directors' fees, non-arm's-length management costs) and any tax base increases
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add only expenses that are economically connected to the Luxembourg PE activity; head-office costs are deductible only to the extent contractually allocated and arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Report de pertes antérieures / Loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable losses brought forward from prior years; amount used in the current year and remaining balance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Luxembourg PE may use available non-resident loss carryforward allocated to the PE if continuity of activity and ownership are preserved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Régime de participation / Dividend exemption
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt dividends and capital gains, with details of the 10% minimum participation and 12-month holding period or equivalent instrument
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Participation exemption applies only to the Luxembourg PE if the holding is attributable to the PE in an economically real manner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 13 - IP Box / Intellectual property relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 80% exempt portion of net qualifying IP income (patents, software, copyrighted software, research-based intellectual assets) after economic substance computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim the IP box only through a Luxembourg PE that holds economically significant risks, staff, assets, and decision-making functions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 15 - Montant de l'impôt / Tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base, municipal business tax base, corporate income tax, solidarity surcharge, deducted tax credits, and resulting tax due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute Luxembourg-source tax only on the PE income; foreign tax credits are not applicable unless a Luxembourg treaty or domestic unilateral relief applies to the PE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic tax increase of up to 10% plus monthly late-interest on the assessed tax; failure after formal reminder leads to ex officio assessment, administrative fines, and loss of favorable regimes; deliberate under-declaration may attract criminal sanctions and fines up to EUR 250,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (standard Luxembourg withholding tax on distributed profits to non-resident and resident shareholders); reduced to 0% for qualifying EU parent-subsidiary directive distributions and for substantial participation relief where the parent holds >=10% or an exemption certificate is granted; treaty rates commonly 0%, 5% or 15% depending on the jurisdiction
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment of a cross-border dividend, the non-resident shareholder must (1) obtain an official tax residency certificate (TRC) from its jurisdiction of residence; (2) produce to the Luxembourg paying agent a completed beneficial-ownership declaration, identifying ultimate recipients and absence of agency/conduit arrangement; (3) invoke the applicable double-taxation agreement (DTA) or EU Directive 2011/96/EU through the simplified source-relief procedure or, where already deducted, file for refund with the Administration des contributions directes; (4) retain the TRC, ownership documentation, and underlying holding evidence for at least five years to withstand audit scrutiny
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes no withholding tax on outbound royalties and no withholding tax on interest paid to non-resident companies; therefore statutory rates are 0% for both categories, and treaty rates are generally 0% or modest residual rates (e.g. 10% for certain royalties under select treaties), but no Luxembourg source tax is levied in practice on arm's-length payments to beneficial owners.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000,000 (country-by-country reporting threshold for multinational groups); Luxembourg does not impose a separate statutory Local File / Master File threshold, but the tax administration may require contemporaneous OECD-compliant TP documentation whenever related-party transactions materially affect the taxable base; in practice, prepare a Local File when annual controlled transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000 or when management/administrative service fees are invoiced intercompany
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no dedicated Economic Substance Regulations in the Caribbean-ESR style, but robust economic substance is a decisive condition for treaty benefits, participation exemption, IP box access, and avoidance of GAAR/ATAD recharacterization; the SARL must evidence real office, autonomous board decisions, qualified staff, transactional risk control, client-facing operational functions, and local bank accounts to prevent classification as a letterbox vehicle.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing incomplete or false corporate income tax returns, deleting taxable revenues received through Stripe/Wise, using fictitious expenses, or disguising bookkeeping fees as company loans in order to avoid Luxembourg corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-assessment of the full taxable base, monthly late interest, 10% late-payment surcharge, administrative fines up to EUR 250,000, and criminal exposure to imprisonment from one month to five years under the Luxembourg General Tax Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns incur joint civil liability for the recovered corporate tax; the corporate veil may be pierced, allowing seizure of personal assets, travel bans pending criminal investigation, and disqualification from exercising corporate board functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the outsourced virtual CFO business with zero local staff, no physical office in Luxembourg, no Luxembourg bank account, and passing management fees through the SARL only as a payment routing conduit for foreign principals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of GAAR/ATAD and the Luxembourg abuse-of-law doctrine; tax authority recharacterizes the payments as taxable Luxembourg-source income, denies treaty relief and participation exemption, reassesses up to six years, and imposes a surcharge of up to 50% of the corrected tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who deliberately maintain a letterbox structure can be ordered by a Luxembourg court to compensate the tax administration personally for lost revenue; travel restrictions and passport surrender are available in serious audit and criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / CDD Failures and Money Laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving client funds through Stripe/Billing or Wise without conducting customer due diligence, maintaining fragmented ledgers, concealing beneficial ownership, or commingling client trust funds with the SARL's operating funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the Luxembourg AML law of 12 November 2004, as amended, ranging up to EUR 250,000 or 10% of annual turnover for serious breaches; laundering proceeds attracts criminal fines and imprisonment of up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for AML breaches are personally and criminally liable; courts may impose confiscation orders on personal assets, prohibit leaving Luxembourg, and bar the director from practicing as a regulated accountant or CFO advisor.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging a non-arm's-length management fee to a foreign affiliate, under-invoicing virtual CFO services, recording financing from a related party at artificial interest rates, or failing to prepare contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation for cross-border intercompany transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment to taxable income at the arm's-length price, payment of the tax shortfall plus late interest, administrative penalty of 10% of the adjustment where documentation is absent, and potential requalification of loans into equity under thin-capitalization principles.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve demonstrably aberrant pricing without economic analysis are liable for the additional tax and interest if they fail to act as prudent persons; serious noncompliance combined with personal benefit may lead to civil restitution, travel bans, and criminal sanctions for deliberate tax evasion.
